tips.title: Mastering Panel Line Scribing with RB Productions
tips.text: For deep, crisp panel lines, use RB Productions scribing tools. Hold the tool like a pencil, not a pen. Apply firm, steady pressure perpendicular to the surface. Start from one end and let the tool's edge bite into the plastic. Use the 0.3mm tool for most kits, switching to 0.5mm for thicker plastic. Once done, carefully clean up any burrs with a sharp hobby knife.

tips.title: Photo-Etch Bending with Eduard's ProMarkers
tips.text: Eduard's ProMarkers are perfect for bending photo-etch parts. Heat the part with a hairdryer, then use the marker to press and hold the part in place until it cools. For tight radii, use the small end, and for larger curves, use the wider end. Be patient; it may take a few attempts to get the right bend.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning: The Soak and Brush Method
tips.text: Clean your Iwata airbrush needle regularly to prevent clogs. Soak it in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for 15 minutes, then scrub it gently with a soft toothbrush. Rinse with water and dry thoroughly. Repeat this process after every 2-3 hours of use or whenever you switch paints.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs. Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Tamiya tape is great for masking large, smooth surfaces, while Kabuki tape is better for intricate, curved details. For best results, use both tapes together. Apply Tamiya tape first, then use Kabuki tape to mask complex shapes or fine edges. Once painted, carefully remove both tapes, starting from a corner.

tips.title: Sanding Stick Progression for Smooth Surfaces
tips.text: Use a progression of sanding sticks to achieve a smooth finish. Start with 400-grit for major imperfections, followed by 600-grit for most of the work, and finish with 800-grit for a mirror-like surface. Wet-sand using water or a suitable lubricant, applying light, even pressure. Inspect your progress frequently to avoid over-sanding.
